evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents Applied-branded examples and period St. Louis Music Supply catalog advertisements from 1968. The same research identifies numerous OEM rebrandings, while exact first-production timing remains an early-1968 working date rather than a fully closed chronology.

Tone Machines states that Banshee Fuzz was available under Applied and Nomad brands and was made by Applied Audio, but manufacturing dates remain unknown. The circuit relationship to the FT-100 is useful family evidence, not a production-date anchor.

Tone Machines identifies Rogue Fuzz as made by Applied Audio and describes it as closely related to the Banshee with an additional gain stage. Nomad is one marketed state, so the label is not the factory identity.

Effects Database catalogs Applied Big Bass and relates it to Conrad Bass Hawk and Goya Boom Box. The model-level maker wording conflicts with the stronger current Applied Audio evidence using Products Inc., so the archive preserves this as a research-grade Applied family association rather than a public lineage claim.

Tone Machines reports a 1969 Conrad effect set, including Bass Hawk, built by Applied Audio. This is stronger than enclosure similarity and is retained as an Applied OEM state, but the cited catalog window does not by itself establish every surviving specimen's exact build date.

Tone Machines states that Goya added Boom Box in 1968 and places post-1966 Goya effects in the Applied Audio production branch. The evidence is strong family evidence but the current record stops short of a public promotion for the entire Goya dirt line.

Tone Machines lists Fury Box among Goya effects added in 1968 and states that post-1966 Goya effects were made in the US by Applied Audio Products Inc. Because the exact product-level documentation is less direct than for Panther Box, this remains research-only.
Tone Machines states that Goya added Power Box in the following year, 1969, and characterizes it as an early LPB-1 copy within the Applied branch. Exact catalog/specimen reconciliation remains open.
